title: PostgreSQL internals, Part 1: how a row is stored on disk
tldr: How PostgreSQL lays a table out on disk: files and forks, the 8 kB page with its line pointers, the 23-byte row header, null bitmap and alignment padding, and TOAST for large values. Then measuring real table sizes, ordering columns to cut padding, per-column TOAST settings, what breaks at 10 times the data, and how to choose a layout in design interviews.
